name: mapk-signalling
title: MAPK signalling as a Bigraphical Reactive System
lead:
The MAP-kinase cascade is the canonical signal-transduction relay in
mammalian cells. This investigation ports that biology onto a bigraph —
molecules nested in compartments (place graph) and MEK·substrate bonds on a
shared edge (link graph) — and drives it with rewrite rules under Gillespie
SSA. It is the workbench home of the original pbg-reactive-system live demo.

at_a_glance.role: Reproduces the prior live demo — runs the MAPK BRS under Gillespie SSA and surfaces its basic systems (bigraph, rules, time series, snapshots, animation).

how_to_read:
Open the mapk-brs-basics study. `report.verdict` is the headline; the five
visualizations reproduce the prior live demo's panels. Open a chart when you
want the detail behind a behavior test.

glossary.definition: Bigraphical Reactive System — a bigraph plus redex→reactum rewrite rules (Milner 2009).
The nesting/containment structure of a bigraph (molecules inside compartments).
The connectivity structure of a bigraph (here, the MEK·substrate catalytic bond).
Stochastic simulation algorithm — exact sampling of reaction waits from per-match propensities.

biological_story:
The MAP-kinase cascade relays extracellular signals to the nucleus. This
investigation models its last catalytic step. In the cytoplasm, MEK binds a
free ERK (forming a MEK·pERK complex on the link graph), then dissociates to
release phospho-ERK; nuclear phosphatases dephosphorylate. Phospho-ERK
translocates through the nuclear pore complex into the nucleus, while ERK and
pERK also shuttle between the cytoplasm and the ER lumen. Rendered as a
bigraph, the place graph nests these molecules inside compartments
(Cell ⊃ Cytoplasm ⊃ {Nucleus, ERLumen}) and rewrite rules under Gillespie SSA
drive the cycle. The member study surfaces the basic systems the demo showed:
the initial bigraph, the rule catalog, the population time series, and the
structural snapshots and animation of pERK entering the nucleus.
question:
Can the MAPK signalling cycle be expressed as a Milner-style Bigraphical
Reactive System and reproduce, under Gillespie SSA, the spatial signalling
behaviour of the prior live demo — MEK·ERK complex formation and phospho-ERK
translocation into the nucleus?
hypothesis:
A single time-stepped BRS process firing seven redex→reactum rewrite rules
over a nested cell bigraph reproduces the qualitative MAPK cycle: complexes
form in the cytoplasm and phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus over the run.

executive.what_is_this:
A single-study demonstration that the Bigraphical Reactive System engine in
this workspace reproduces the MAPK signalling cycle from the prior live demo,
now runnable and inspectable inside the workbench.
executive.verdict:
Reproduced. The MAPK BRS runs under Gillespie SSA and shows MEK·substrate
complex formation and phospho-ERK nuclear translocation; all five behavior
tests pass on a seeded 120-tick run.
executive.verdict_detail:
Qualitative, uncalibrated demonstration — rule rates are illustrative and
the rewrite rules are not mass-conserving, so this validates the engine and
the spatial mechanism, not quantitative MAPK kinetics.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
A Milner-style bigraph with seven rewrite rules reproduces the MAPK cycle's
spatial signalling as emergent stochastic dynamics.
evidence_for: Nuclear phospho-ERK rises from 0 to 144 over a seeded 120-tick run.
MEK·substrate complexes form (0 → 59), the catalytic intermediate.
All five behavior tests pass (translocation, empty-start, complex formation, population growth, run length).
evidence_against: Substrate copies grow over the run — the rules are not mass-conserving, unlike real MAPK turnover.
caveats: Illustrative rate constants; a single seeded trajectory; no calibration or robustness sweep.

studies.name: mapk-brs-basics
studies.title: MAPK BRS basics
studies.question:
Run as a Bigraphical Reactive System under Gillespie SSA, does the MAPK
signalling cycle reproduce the qualitative behaviour of the prior live demo
— MEK·ERK complexes forming in the cytoplasm and phospho-ERK accumulating
in the nucleus by the end of the run?

findings.statement:
Phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus over the run — nucleus pERK rises
from 0 to 144 across 120 ticks (seed 42).

MEK·substrate complexes form during the run — the catalytic intermediate
count rises from 0 to 59, and the nucleus starts empty (0 at t=0).

The MAPK cycle's spatial signalling — cytoplasmic complex formation and
nuclear translocation of phospho-ERK — emerges from seven local
redex→reactum rewrite rules fired under Gillespie SSA, reproducing the
prior live demo qualitatively.
findings.next_action:
Add a mass-conserving rule variant and a multi-seed robustness sweep to
move from qualitative demonstration toward a calibrated model.

studies.claim:
Run as a Bigraphical Reactive System under Gillespie SSA, the MAPK cycle
reproduces the prior live demo: MEK·substrate complexes form in the
cytoplasm and phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus (0 → 144 over 120 ticks).

biological_validation.basis: Qualitatively correct (nuclear pERK accumulation, complex formation) but uncalibrated and non-conserving, so not a quantitative match.

regression_compatibility.basis: The composite builds and the 120-tick baseline runs cleanly under Gillespie SSA; all 5 behavior tests pass.

explanatory_gain.basis: Demonstrates that a Milner-style BRS reproduces the MAPK cycle's spatial signalling as emergent rewrite dynamics.

derived.insight:
Phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus over the run — nucleus pERK rises
from 0 to 144 across 120 ticks (seed 42).
